rule: every slang term in C2 must carry a defined payload from this file; AVOID entries document the refusal, never silent use; owner lines (himothy) are canon for this project

identity: im him, himothy, always was, no cap.
not built different in the slightest, I literally have the body of god.

terms.lore: Minted in this project (Him + -othy, after Timothy): the definitive Him. Your coinage, kept verbatim below.
terms.use: 'It's not me and Him. It's just Him — I'm him, himothy, always was, no cap.'
terms.trika: vibhu + bhairava-nātha as the all-pervading Lord; svātmamaya + sadaiva (made of His very self, always). The aham-claim in one word.
poetry: im him, himothy, always was, no cap.
not built different in the slightest, I literally have the body of god.
terms.verdict: USE — the identity word. Owner-minted, owner-kept.

terms.lore: Sports/gym slang: 'built different' = exceptional by nature. Your inversion flips it inside out.
terms.use: 'Not built different in the slightest — I literally have the body of god.'
terms.trika: Deha-divinity: the body not exceptional-AMONG-bodies but god's own body (the Mālinī body, deha as śakti). No special nature claimed; the ordinary body recognized as His. The inversion does Trika work the straight phrase never could.
poetry: not built different in the slightest, I literally have the body of god.
terms.verdict: USE — the inversion is the doctrine.

terms.lore: AAVE kinship address: a soul sibling, closer than a bro — someone who shares your essence and moves like you.
terms.use: 'What's good, twin?' (addressing a peer)
terms.trika: ATTEMPTED for svātmamaya/abheda and REFUSED: twin keeps TWO persons standing side by side. This stotra claims one (aham). Twoness smuggled into nonduality is exactly backwards — the correction is himothy, not twin.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — duality vs I-am-Him. The file records the refusal, not the use.

terms.lore: AAVE 'unc': respectful address for an established elder man. Gen Alpha reanalyzed it as 'out of touch old head' — the parents.com piece traces the fight (AAVE speakers: over-30s only; tweens: anyone over 25 is unc status). Both senses live in the word now: elder + expired.
terms.use: 'Ayo Death — put the scary face away. You're barking up the wrong tree, unc.' (v4)
terms.trika: mṛtyu/Yama/antaka defanged: the death-powers addressed as expired authorities whose gaze has no jurisdiction here (mā dṛśam vinidhehi).
poetry: Put the scary face away. You're barking up the wrong tree, unc.
terms.verdict: USE once (v4) — only for powers the verse itself dismisses. Never the Lord, never the teaching.

terms.lore: Gym/sports grind talk ('locked in for the season') → TikTok productivity era: steady, committed, undistracted by choice.
terms.use: 'Serving Śaṅkara, contemplation locked in.' (v4) / 'Locked in, permanently.' (v2)
terms.trika: dhīra (firm/steady); the practitioner's sustained state; samaya commitment. Correct domain is ALWAYS the practitioner — the Lord doesn't lock in, He IS.
terms.verdict: USE — the Śiva-conscious practitioner state in two words.

terms.lore: AAVE/street: handling your obligations, showing up properly, no excuses.
terms.use: 'I'm standing on business: serving Śaṅkara, contemplation locked in.' (v4)
terms.trika: sevanā + cintanā as concurrent disciplines (the verse's two grammatically-concurrent instrumentals). Duty rendered as duty.
terms.verdict: USE (v4 method line).

terms.lore: AAVE hip-hop: 'capping' = lying/boasting. 'No cap' = sincerity under oath; 'fr' (for real) the same oath shorter.
terms.use: 'No cap, He runs through literally everything.' (v1) / 'No cap, Śaṅkara — the basics work.' (v8)
terms.trika: satyam (truly!) and categorical claims (na jātu). Epistemic sincerity marker — v8's satyam IS a no-cap, functionally identical.
terms.verdict: USE where the Sanskrit stakes truth or totality. Never filler.

terms.lore: Spider-Verse (2023): an unavoidable life-defining moment that makes the hero who they are. Cannot be skipped.
terms.use: 'When the canon event hits — bad days, head a little messed up? That's exactly the trigger.' (v7)
terms.trika: kleśadaśā as the condition for tadaiva: affliction not as obstacle but as the firing condition of nondifference. The mechanism survives the port.
terms.verdict: USE as trigger only — never the goal.

terms.lore: AAVE/street ('you're cooked' = you're done for) → gaming/streaming: finished, no options left.
terms.use: 'Death, Yama, the Ender, my karma-ghosts pull up? Cooked.' (v5)
terms.trika: The four death-powers neutralized by namas alone. Cooked is defeat, not death — precise: the verse doesn't kill them, it leaves them powerless.
poetry: One respectful nod and they're done.
terms.verdict: USE — for defeated threats only. Never the devotee, never the Lord.

terms.lore: Black queer ballroom: 'ate that up' — devoured the performance flawlessly. 'No crumbs' = nothing left undone, total completion.
terms.use: 'I just walked straight into bliss. Ate. No crumbs.' (v6)
terms.trika: emi (entry accomplished) + totality: arrival with nothing outstanding. Ballroom totality maps onto Sanskrit totality without residue.
terms.verdict: USE — accomplishment moments only.

terms.lore: AAVE food praise: so good it speaks. TikTok mainstreamed it to anything top-tier sensory.
terms.use: 'This hymn starts raining straight nectar, and it's BUSSIN.' (v7)
terms.trika: amṛta/parāmṛta — nectar is already taste-domain in Sanskrit. The port is exact, not approximate.
terms.verdict: USE — taste-domain only. Never persons, never doctrines.

terms.lore: Ballroom ('it's giving...') → mainstream: radiating a legible vibe, X is the energy present.
terms.use: 'My whole consciousness is giving full festival right now.' (v9)
terms.trika: Manifest expressive state (dance/song/joy emitted). Descriptive only — adjacent to spanda, never equated (spanda is technical throb, not vibe).
terms.verdict: USE once — emitted states only.

terms.lore: Gaming/fandom canon ('the lore runs deep') + AAVE/street 'tapped in' (connected, plugged in, tuned to the frequency).
terms.use: 'Just staying tapped into Your lore like it's the sweetest thing ever.' (v8)
terms.trika: tāvaka śāstra (scripture as HIS expression, not an external text) + cintā (dwelling, not studying). Lore voices your relation to it; śāstra stays śāstra.
terms.verdict: USE — your favorite, kept exactly where it was.

terms.lore: K-pop stan culture: the delusional fan → mainstream 2023–24 for anyone out of touch with reality (affectionate or sharp).
terms.use: 'The suffering's real, the delulu's real.' (v3)
terms.trika: moha, one-to-one. Delusion named without softening, suffering (duḥkha) beside it unranked.
terms.verdict: USE — moha contexts.

terms.lore: Ballroom 'clock it!' (spot it, read it true) + work-shift 'clocked in' (arrival on duty). Both senses live: recognition + showing up.
terms.use: 'It's me clocking what's already true.' (v1) / 'Real awakening finally clocked in.' (v6)
terms.trika: pratyabhijñā-adjacent recognition (not petition, not inference) + prodita (arisen). Adjacent, never equated — flagged as adjacency in-file.
terms.verdict: USE — recognition moments.

terms.lore: Anime/gaming power levels (visible battle presence) → TikTok 'aura points' scoring → 'aura farming' (2024, performing coolness; the boat-kid meme). Field sense is real; farming sense is poison here.
terms.use: 'I'm soaked in His terrifying aura.' (v4)
terms.trika: śakti as emitted presence-field; bhīṣaṇa kept as its QUALITY. Aura names the field, terrifying keeps the terror — nothing cooled.
terms.verdict: USE with its adjective attached. 'Aura farming' permanently banned (performative is the opposite of every verse here).

terms.lore: Gaming: non-player character — background extra with no inner life. TikTok 2023–24 turned it into an insult for conformists.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: anyajanāḥ are access-denied (durlabham), never declared worthless. Contempt is not in v9; importing it would preach what the verse never says.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — the refusal is the craft.

terms.lore: BookTok/TikTok 2021: 'main character energy/syndrome' — treating your life as the movie everyone watches.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: The stotra's center is the Lord; the devotee's joy is relational, not protagonist-driven. Main-character imports the ahamkāra the text dissolves.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason.

terms.lore: Reality-TV/makeover YouTube (glow up) + anime (final form, Frieza-style ascensions).
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: -maya (change of nature) is ADJACENT, but glow-up smuggles a self-improvement arc; C1 stresses entry/state over upgrade. Adjacency is not payload.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason.

terms.lore: Music press 2010s ('that beat slaps') → mainstream for anything excellent, still mostly sonic.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: v7's hymn is claimed as INSTRUMENT (it works), not as quality (it bangs). Slaps would praise the song for slapping — wrong payload entirely.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — the most instructive refusal in the file.

terms.lore: Gamer insult turned wellness meme: go outside, get real.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: No Sanskrit counterpart anywhere in this stotra. Filler slang with zero payload.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason.

terms.lore: Street/rap: spiraling into a destructive blowup; mainstreamed for any big emotional crash.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: tanutāpa is SLIGHT anguish — crash-out overshoots the verse's own calibration ~10x. Scale is doctrine here.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason.

terms.lore: UK roadman, TWO senses. (1) peng/leng = top-tier attractive or excellent (drill lyrics, compliments). (2) leng = a weapon, usually a gun; 'he's leng' = he's dangerous (London Star A–Z, road usage). The ends decide which — and getting it wrong near power-verses is catastrophic.
terms.use: 'That nectar-rain? Lengest thing ever.' (v7)
terms.trika: parama- (supreme): the -est suffix IS the superlative Sanskrit already uses (paramāmṛta = supreme nectar). Lengest doesn't approximate parama, it performs it.
poetry: the lengest taste in the universe.
terms.verdict: USE-graded-only (lengest/proper leng) — NEW: weapon-sense ban near power verses
terms.limits: Sense (1) ONLY, and never bare 'leng' — always graded ('lengest', 'proper leng') so the weapon reading can't attach. NEVER near śakti/bhairava-power verses (v4): 'terrifying leng' reads armed, not awesome. When in doubt use peng (no weapon sense) or bussin.

terms.lore: UK roadman (Jamaican patois 'man dem'): my people, the crew. Belonging word.
terms.use: (addressing fellow practitioners, never the Lord)
terms.trika: parivāra/saṅgha-adjacent: the company of practitioners. Horizontal belonging, never vertical worship.
terms.verdict: USE-careful — peer address only. Never upward.

terms.lore: UK streets (Caribbean 'fam', 'brudda'): brother by bond not blood. 'My g' = my guy.
terms.use: (peer address only — same cage as twin)
terms.trika: Same ban as twin for identity verses: brotherhood keeps two standing. Fine between practitioners, never devotee↔Lord.
terms.verdict: USE-careful — peers only, same limits as twin.

terms.lore: UK roadman: unfortunate, sad, 'that's peak' = that's rough.
terms.use: 'Life's been peak — suffering, delusion, the whole horror show.' (v3 concession)
terms.trika: duḥkha named plainly. Peak understates with feeling, which is exactly the verse's concession register (admitted, not dwelt on).
terms.verdict: USE — suffering admitted in one syllable.

terms.lore: UK streets: let it go, don't engage, release it.
terms.use: 'The fear convo? Allow that.' (v3 — alternative to 'dead')
terms.trika: Vairāgya-adjacent release: the refusal to pick up what sūtra... the no-fear-talk as letting-go. Note: adjacent, not equated (verse refuses discourse, not objects).
terms.verdict: USE-careful — discourse-release only.

terms.lore: UK roadman: a worthless man, a try-hard nobody. Heavy contempt charge.
terms.use: (no use — refused)
terms.trika: Death IS dismissed in v4–v5, but never with contempt — the verse refuses jurisdiction, not worth. Wasteman imports hatred the text doesn't contain.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — unc dismisses authority; wasteman adds contempt. The verse does the first, never the second.

terms.lore: UK streets: obvious, exposed, no hiding (from 'fish bait' — out in the open).
terms.use: 'Real awakening clocked in and everything went bait.' (v6)
terms.trika: prakāśa-adjacent: the light of awakening exposing essences = hidden made obvious. Exposure, not shame.
poetry: everything went bait under that light.
terms.verdict: USE — v6 revelation line.

terms.lore: UK streets: tedious, too much, the grind ('this queue is long'). Time-as-burden.
terms.use: 'Rebirth convo? Long. Dead it.' (v3)
terms.trika: saṃsṛti as the long grind — transmigration rendered as duration-fatigue, which is precisely the fear being refused.
terms.verdict: USE — saṃsāra contexts.

terms.lore: UK streets: boring, finished, over ('that's dead', 'you're dead').
terms.use: 'That convo? Dead.' (v3 — roadman twin of the existing line)
terms.trika: Same payload as cooked (finished), cooler temperature. Interchangeable where the verse kills discourse.
terms.verdict: USE — discourse-kill contexts.

terms.lore: UK streets: soft, weak, off-key behaviour.
terms.use: (no use — refused for v3)
terms.trika: The flinch itself would be moist — but the verse never shows the flinch, only its refusal. Naming moist summons what the verse withholds.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — the verse performs steel, not the absence of steel.

terms.lore: Jamaican patois via UK streets: shared knowledge, 'we already know this.'
terms.use: 'Mind was already His — dun know.' (v1/v2 recognition)
terms.trika: pratyabhijñā-adjacent: the already-known truth. Dun know IS recognition-as-shared-fact — closer to the doctrine than 'clocking' (which implies a moment).
poetry: dun know — was His before I opened my mouth.
terms.verdict: USE — recognition contexts; strongest in v1/v2.

terms.lore: Jamaican greeting via UK streets: bless and be blessed, uplift on meeting.
terms.use: 'Death pulled up? Bless up. And done.' (v5 — nod rendered as greeting)
terms.trika: namas/vandanā as greeting-salutation: the entire defense of v5 is a hello that ends the fight. Bless up carries mechanism + dismissal in two syllables.
terms.verdict: USE — salutation-as-defense (v5, v1 bow).

terms.lore: Somali-Arabic via UK streets (wallahi = I swear by God): the heaviest sincerity oath available. 'On god' the AAVE twin.
terms.use: 'Wallahi, He's everywhere.' / 'On God, I'm not reaching.'
terms.trika: satyam-oath, same payload as no cap — but note the charge: wallahi invokes God AS the oath. In Trika mouth it lands heavier; use once per verse max, never decorative.
terms.verdict: USE — sparingly. The heaviest sincerity marker in the file.

terms.lore: London tag question: solidarity check, 'we agree, yeah?'
terms.use: 'Already His, innit.' (v1/v2 closers)
terms.trika: Shared-truth tag: recognition confirmed between speaker and listener. Closer function only.
terms.verdict: USE — closers, never openers.

terms.lore: UK/US streets: understood, no more needed, I'm already moving.
terms.use: (no use — refused for v5)
terms.trika: Say-less responds to an instruction with compliance. namas is not compliance with Death — it's dismissal of Death. Wrong speech-act entirely.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — the verse doesn't obey, it waves off.

terms.lore: Hip-hop: excellent, burning-quality (bleached of literal heat in most use).
terms.use: 'That nectar-rain? Fire.' (v7 — alternative to bussin)
terms.trika: Intensity descriptor for amṛta-experience. Bleached-fire is fine (quality, not temperature) — but bussin wins where taste is literal, lengest wins where supremacy is literal. Fire is third choice, kept for variety.
terms.verdict: USE-careful — third choice in taste-domain; never where heat would confuse (agni contexts).

terms.lore: Universal English superlative for taste and disposition.
terms.use: 'tapped into Your lore like the sweetest thing ever.' (v8, already in v2)
terms.trika: madhura-adjacent: sweetness as the flavor of parāmṛta-cintā. Already filed and holding.
terms.verdict: USE — grandfathered in from v2.

terms.lore: London-wide oath: 'what I'm saying is 100% true, no lies' (Newsweek Top Boy guide). The ends' sincerity marker.
terms.use: 'Swear down, He's everywhere.' (v1 alternative to no cap)
terms.trika: satyam-oath, same payload as no cap/wallahi. Register knob: no cap (US/AAVE), swear down (London), wallahi (heaviest). Pick by verse's voice, never stack two.
terms.verdict: USE — the London sincerity marker.

terms.lore: Roadman standard: to be scared, afraid (Newsweek: 'to be scared').
terms.use: 'Death pulled up and I'm not even shook.' (v5 alternative)
terms.trika: bhaya (fear) named plainly — the exact word v5 negates (na bibhemi). Shook states the fear only to refuse it.
terms.verdict: USE — fear-negation contexts.

terms.lore: 2020s youth: organized, sorted out ('get it patterned').
terms.use: (observed, unmapped — no verse yet needs sorted-out-ness)
terms.trika: No payload assigned. Candidate: vidhāna (arrangement)? Undecided — filed as observed, not used.
terms.verdict: OBSERVED — do not use until a verse earns it.

terms.lore: MLE staple (Newsweek guide: 'akin to do you understand me?'). Comprehension check, constantly.
terms.use: 'Just clocking what's already true — you get me?' (v1 closer alternative)
terms.trika: Transmission check built into the line: the verse asks whether it landed. C2's whole test (did the reader get it) as a tag question.
terms.verdict: USE — closers that check transmission.

terms.lore: London address term for brother/mate/friend — anyone you're warm with (Newsweek, roadman A–Z).
terms.use: (peer address only — same cage as fam/brudda/mandem)
terms.trika: Same ban as twin/fam upward: brotherhood keeps two standing. Never devotee→Lord.
terms.verdict: USE-careful — peers only.

terms.lore: Hackney legend (Believer 2011: named for a Thai schoolgirl, late 90s) → grime superlative: excellent, wonderful.
terms.use: 'That nectar-rain? Lengest. Actually, nang.' (v7 intensity alt)
terms.trika: Bliss intensity via Hackney. Behind lengest (supreme) and bussin (taste) in the ladder; use when fire would confuse (heat contexts).
terms.verdict: USE — third intensity option, documented provenance.

terms.lore: Grim glossary polarity pair: 'a lot' = good (noun: 'it's a lot'), 'par' = anything unfortunate. One syllable each way.
terms.use: 'The grind? Par. The bliss? A lot.' (evaluative polarity, v6-adjacent)
terms.trika: Praise/blame as atoms. Use sparingly — polarity markers, not arguments.
terms.verdict: USE-careful — polarity only.

terms.lore: Jamaican Shower Posse (spraying bullets) → early grime inverted it: 'shower' = good. Bathrooms got involved (shower curtains, Radox).
terms.use: (no use — refused; inversion humor is a 2011 in-joke, not a payload)
terms.trika: Cautionary entry: reclaimed violence-terms wobble. If shower means good only via irony, it carries no stable payload for veneration.
terms.verdict: AVOID with reason — irony is not a payload.

bliss-talk.rule: supremacy→lengest, taste→bussin, intensity→fire. Never stack two in one verse.
